subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - postcall recap
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jake Porter <jake.porter@finlytics.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: p95/p99 end-to-end latency targets (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Jake / Maya —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned on the performance qualification scope:

Summary of Finlytics requirements (as discussed):
- End-to-end p95 latency target: <= 200 ms
- End-to-end p99 latency target: <= 400 ms
- Typical request profile: chat-style prompts, avg prompt length ~120 tokens, response length ~280 tokens (streaming enabled)
- Concurrency target: sustained 200 concurrent user requests (peaks to 400 for short bursts)
- Throughput: ~2M tokens/day (~25 TPS sustained across the fleet)
- Streaming: required (customers expect incremental tokens within 150ms of generation start)

What we heard about your current provider: you mentioned p95 ~250ms, p99 ~550ms in production for comparable payloads — please correct me if my notes are off.

Proposed qualification plan / next steps:
1) We’ll run a controlled performance run against our hosted API using your representative prompt set (you provide ~25 sample prompts and the expected token lengths).
2) Redwood will supply a short test harness + instructions and run one internal baseline with our default hosted config (we’ll measure p95/p99 end-to-end including streaming behavior).
3) If baseline looks promising, we’ll iterate on batching/quantization and a dedicated test run tuned to your concurrency profile.
4) Share results and recommended config; if you want we can do a 2-week evaluation with a committed Dedicated pool for apples-to-apples comparison.

Attachments: postcall-sla-requirements.pdf (summary of SLAs and test checklist).

Please confirm the sample prompts and whether the concurrency/throughput numbers above match your production needs. Also, if you can share a small anonymized sample of current-provider latency logs (p95/p99 by endpoint) that would be helpful — I can point Marissa to them and she’ll triage.

I’ll follow up with the test harness link once I hear back.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference
From: Jake Porter <jake.porter@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: p95/p99 end-to-end latency targets (hosted vs current provider)

Thanks Laura — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming the numbers you captured are accurate for our target workload. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The p95/p99 targets are end-to-end from our app -> provider -> client streaming; so they must include any proxying and network overheads you would expect in a hosted deployment.
- Our current provider numbers (production averages over last 30 days): p95 ~250ms, p99 ~550ms (aggregated across our standard chat endpoint); during peak incidents p99 can spike over 800ms.
- We can provide the sample prompts — I’ll attach a CSV with 30 representative prompts and a short set of expected response characteristics.
- Attached: finlytics-currentprovider-latency-logs.csv (30-day aggregates) and a short note on request headers we use that might affect routing.

We’re very interested in seeing how Redwood performs on streaming latencies (especially the time to first token and token inter-arrival latency).

One ask: can you include in the baseline run the time-to-first-token (TTFT) metric and per-token inter-arrival stats for the streaming session? That will help us match the UX.

Happy to set up a demo/test window next week.

— Jake
Jake Porter
VP Product, Finlytics
jake.porter@finlytics.com | (617) 555-0890
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jake Porter <jake.porter@finlytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: p95/p99 end-to-end latency targets (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Jake / Laura —

Thanks for the logs and prompt set, Jake. Quick engineering note and proposed test plan from our side:

Engineering clarifications we’ll need to run an apples-to-apples test:
- Exact request path you use (direct API vs proxied through CDN). If proxied, please include typical added latency.
- TLS termination point (we may be able to mirror your config).
- Expected avg and max sequence lengths (you mentioned avg prompt 120 tokens / response ~280 tokens). Please confirm distribution if you have it.

Planned baseline run (hosted API):
1) Run harness with your 30 prompts at 5 concurrency levels: 10, 50, 100, 200, 400 sustained for 5 minutes each.
2) Measure: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, time-to-first-token (TTFT), token inter-arrival median/95/99, and error rates.
3) Capture streaming traces and provide logs + flamegraph of server-side latencies (kernel scheduling, batching wait time, model inference).
4) Compare to your provided current-provider aggregates and create a delta report.

Notes on streaming metrics: we can instrument the harness to emit both TTFT and per-token latencies. For streaming TF/TPS behavior we’ll include a 1s startup steady-state window to measure token pacing.

Related links: perf runbook and harness instructions: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/XXXXXXXX/perf-runbook
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DL-2027-0043

If that plan looks good I’ll queue up the hosted baseline run this Thursday (22 Apr) at 09:00 PT — Laura, can you confirm that time with the Finlytics team?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
